newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MILAN LOSE 3-1 AT LOWLY VERONA, SLIP TO 10TH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN LOSE 3-1 AT LOWLY VERONA, SLIP TO 10TH.

text.p: Milan's fading hopes of retaining their title all but disappeared on Sunday after a humiliating 3-1 defeat at second-from-bottom Verona left them 10th in the serie A table.
Arrigo Sacchi's side have now lost seven league matches this season -- as many as they have won -- and lie eleven points behind leaders Juventus, 3-1 winners over bottom club Reggiana.
Juve's Michele Padovano, playing against his old club, scored one goal and made another to keep the European champions four points clear at the top with 36 points from 18 matches.
Second-place Sampdoria kept Juve within their sights after coming from 2-1 down to defeat Perugia 5-2 thanks to their prolific front-line partnership of Vincenzo Montella and Roberto Mancini.

Both strikers scored twice to take veteran Mancini's career total to 138 goals in serie A and lift Montella to the top of this season's first division goalscoring standings with 13 goals from 12 matches.

Vicenza, convincing 3-2 winners over Fiorentina, moved into third on 30 points, one point ahead of Internazionale Milan, who needed a second-half penalty from French playmaker Youri Djorkaeff to scrape a 1-1 draw against Udinese at the San Siro stadium.
Bologna lie fifth on 28 points following their 2-1 win at Lazio, a defeat that leaves the Rome side dangerously close to the relegation zone.
Unfancied Atalanta, unbeaten since November, crushed Cagliari 4-1 to climb to sixth on 27 points.
Napoli recovered from the first-half dismissal of midfielder Francesco Turrini to break Parma's six-match unbeaten run with a 2-1 victory.
